acme-platform: Hey, after we set up the interface endpoint for api.redwood.example the service calls intermittently time out from our private subnets. Happens only for a subset of instances.
acme-platform: curl just hangs (connect timeout). traceroute shows traffic going to our NAT GW rather than the interface endpoint ENI.
andrea: Thanks — can you paste the traceroute and a curl run (with --resolve if possible)? Also which subnets are associated to the endpoint?
acme-platform: sure, repro steps: from app host in subnet-10a `curl -v https://api.redwood.example` -> timeout. traceroute: `1 10.0.0.1 (eni-abc) 1.2 ms` then `2 10.1.0.1 (nat-xyz) 12 ms` then internet path.
acme-platform: interface endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce-012345) is attached to subnets 10a and 10b. Private DNS enabled.
andrea: do you have custom DNS resolvers or Route 53 conditional forwarding? If Private DNS is enabled the endpoint's hosted zone should resolve the service name to the interface ENI IPs in those subnets.
acme-platform: we do have a private resolver in VPC that forwards to a central resolver in another account. That resolver has conditional forwarders for several domains.
mike: can you run `dig +short api.redwood.example` from a broken host vs a working host and paste output? Also `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-012345 --query 'DnsEntries'` would help.
acme-platform: broken host dig -> 52.94.23.11 (public), working host dig -> 10.0.5.12 (eni-ip). aws CLI shows two DnsEntries pointing to the ENI IPs.
andrea: OK that indicates DNS resolution divergence. Broken hosts are resolving to public IP (so traffic goes out natgw). Why would the resolver return public IP? maybe the central resolver is not forwarding queries to the VPC resolver or caching public answer.
andrea: can you show `tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 53` while doing dig on the broken host?
acme-platform: tcpdump shows queries going to 10.0.0.2 (our custom resolver) and the response is 52.94.23.11. central resolver logs show NXDOMAIN hit then fallback to public -> cached public A.
mike: ah — this is classic split-horizon resolution break: your central forwarder isn't configured to forward the AWS VPC endpoint private hosted zone (the zonename is something like vpce.amazonaws.com hosted zone). When Private DNS is enabled, AWS expects VPC resolver (the .2 IP) to answer with ENI IPs. But since queries are forwarded off-vpc, central returns public.
mike: workaround: add a forwarding rule on your central resolver for the 3rd-party AWS zone to forward queries back to VPC resolver IPs for that VPC or enable conditional forwarding per VPC. Another quick check: from the broken host `dig @10.0.0.2 api.redwood.example` vs `dig @169.254.169.253` (VPC resolver) to compare.
acme-platform: tried `dig @169.254.169.253 api.redwood.example` -> returns 10.0.5.12 as expected. `dig @10.0.0.2 api.redwood.example` -> public IP.
andrea: great reproduction. Two follow-ups: 1) firewall / security groups must allow host->endpoint ENI on 443. 2) confirm route tables don't have more-specific route to NAT for service IP ranges.
acme-platform: SGs allow 443 to 10.0.0.0/8. route table default route to NAT for 0.0.0.0/0. No explicit route to the ENI ips.
mike: interface endpoints are reached via prefix routed by AWS platform; you shouldn't need a route to the specific ENI IPs — but you must hit ENI IPs directly once DNS resolves them. The core issue is DNS.
mike: there's another edge case — if your host has source/dest check disabled and there's an inline proxy doing SNAT, or if your NAT appliance responds to ARP for the ENI IP ranges (rare), you could see hairpin. But given dig shows public IP, let's fix resolver first.
andrea: confirm TLS: when you did curl against the public IP did you see SNI mismatch or cert for redwood? Public IP will terminate elsewhere and likely SNI mismatch. Can you run `openssl s_client -connect 52.94.23.11:443 -servername api.redwood.example`?
acme-platform: running that returns cert for other service and handshake fails in app (500s intermittently).
mike: that confirms requests hitting wrong backend. Please update your central resolver with a conditional forwarder for the AWS VPC endpoint zone (or disable forwarding for that domain so VPC resolver answers directly). If you need a short-term patch, add an /etc/hosts entry on the broken hosts mapping api.redwood.example -> 10.0.5.12 (not recommended long term).
acme-platform: we've added a conditional forwarder to point to 169.254.169.253 for that zone. Testing now...
acme-platform: retest: dig -> 10.0.5.12 ; curl -> 200 OK; openssl shows correct cert and SNI. :thumbsup:
andrea: awesome! final checklist for you: - keep conditional forwarder or configure Route 53 resolver rules (inbound endpoints) so central resolver knows to forward to VPC. - review caching TTLs on central resolver to avoid stale public answers. - confirm security group for endpoint only allows our service origins.
mike: I'll add a note to our troubleshooting KB: "Private DNS + central resolvers: ensure forwarders for vpce hosted zones or bypass central resolver for VPC-specific services". acme-platform, please re-open if you see flake after TTL expiry.
acme-platform: thanks all, will monitor for a day and report back. very helpful.
support-bot: Incident follow-up: tag=private-connectivity; severity=low; owner=andrea; linked-ticket=SUP-2147
acme-platform: confirmed stable after 24h, marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
